title: feat(i18n,plugin-calendar,plugin-timeline): the calendar and the timeline start the week on the locale's first day (objectui#11675)
body:
Fixes #11675
Clause-②: yes

The calendar and the timeline now start the week on the first day of the week of the user's locale, as ruling B on the card asks (the maintainer's 「同意」, recorded in comment 6010771237): under `en-US` both start on Sunday, under `en-GB` or `zh-CN` both start on Monday, from the locale's week info. Before this, the calendar always started on Sunday and the timeline's "This week" always on Monday. No setting is added: the first day comes from the tag each component already formats its dates with.

Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01FngvPpdrnhHMdHHq6vwwju` (dispatched os-dev, seat `domain:ui#2`, claim comment 6012945073).

## Premise check, on `origin/main` at `daa7caf`

- Calendar: the Sunday start was in `CalendarView.tsx`: `getMonthDays` padded the first row by `firstDay.getDay()`, `getWeekStart` stepped back by `getDay()`, the month view's weekday heads ran from a reference Sunday, and a span wrapping into a new row was titled on `getDay() === 0`. `getWeekStart` also fed the week view's columns and the header's week range.
- Timeline: `ObjectTimeline.tsx`'s bucket bounds used `startOfWeek = today - ((now.getDay() + 6) % 7) * day`, a Monday start.
- No shared helper existed: `git grep` for `weekInfo`, `getWeekInfo`, `firstDayOfWeek` and `weekStartsOn` under `packages/*/src` answered nothing, with the control word `firstDay` (a local in `getMonthDays`) answering.
- The premise holds. The only other week-related site is the gantt variant's `week` axis, which counts plan weeks from the axis's first day and does not snap to a weekday by design (its own docblock in `renderer.tsx` says so). It is left as it is (see Acceptance notes).

## What changed

**`@object-ui/i18n` exports `firstDayOfWeek(locale)` and `WeekdayIndex`** (`src/utils/first-day-of-week.ts`). It returns 0 to 6 as `Date.prototype.getDay` numbers weekdays, which is also react-day-picker's `weekStartsOn`. Both plugins already import this package, and it hosts `useDisplayLocale`, the locale both format with.

- Engine first: `Intl.Locale`'s `getWeekInfo()`, else the `weekInfo` accessor (ISO 1 to 7, 7 is Sunday), so a `-u-fw-` keyword is honoured.
- Measured engine support: Node 22.22 (V8 12.4, the test and CI runtime) has the accessor only. Chromium 141 (the preinstalled Playwright build) has both. Firefox was not measured: no Firefox build is in this container.
- Where the engine has neither: CLDR's `weekData` first-day table, keyed by the tag's region or the one `maximize()` gives it (`en` reads `US`, `zh` reads `CN`). An unlisted region reads Monday, CLDR's world default `001`. This is the deterministic fallback, and the tests cover it.
- The table transcribes one CLDR release, declared in the source as `WEEK_DATA_CLDR` (`48`, the release CI's floating `22.x` Node ships), and was generated from Node's ICU. Engines carry their own week data, and it differs: CLDR 48 moved Iceland to a Sunday start, and Chromium 141 starts `AE` on Saturday where Node's CLDR 46, 47 and 48 all start it on Monday. That is why the engine's answer wins wherever there is one. A parity case re-derives the table against the running engine, region by region (see Patch round 1).
- A malformed tag (`en_US`) throws `Intl.Locale`'s `RangeError`, as `toLocaleDateString` does for the same tag in the same render. No day is guessed.

**`@object-ui/plugin-calendar`.** `CalendarView` computes `weekStart = firstDayOfWeek(effectiveLocale)` once (the authored `locale` prop, else the display locale) and passes it to every site:

- the month grid's leading days and its weekday heads;
- the title day of a span that wraps into a new row;
- the week view's columns and the header's week range;
- the date popover, through `weekStartsOn`.

The popover used to take date-fns's own `weekStartsOn`. That is not CLDR's for every tag: date-fns has no `es-MX`, so the tag reads `es`, a Monday start, where CLDR starts Mexico's week on Sunday. It also read `enUS`, a Sunday start, until the locale loaded. The new memo dependencies include `weekStart`.

**`@object-ui/plugin-timeline`.** `ObjectTimeline` reads `useDisplayLocale()`, the same hook its renderer formats with, and starts "This week" on `firstDayOfWeek(displayLocale)`. The bounds block was rewritten as local midnights stepped on the local calendar (`daysFromToday(n)`), which includes `tomorrow`, in place of `today + n * 86400000`. Across a DST change the old arithmetic missed "Tomorrow" and put the first day of next week into "This week". Measured in the driven zone pin (America/Los_Angeles, Sunday 8 March 2026): the 9th now reads "Tomorrow" and the 15th "Next week". This is a published defect inside the block this change rewrites, so it is corrected here rather than filed (see Acceptance notes).

**Built-declaration reading (Clause-②):** `packages/i18n/dist/utils/first-day-of-week.d.ts` declares `export type WeekdayIndex = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;` and `export declare function firstDayOfWeek(locale: string): WeekdayIndex;`. `dist/index.d.ts` re-exports both. So the helper widens the package's public surface, and `Clause-②: yes` stands.

**Docs:** the i18n README (a "The first day of the week" subsection), the calendar and timeline READMEs, and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` / `plugin-timeline.mdx`. **Changeset:** `.changeset/11675-week-start-from-locale.md`, `minor` for the three packages.

## Tests

- New `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/firstDayOfWeek-11675.test.ts` (14 cases):
  - the card's pins on both paths, plus a Saturday and a Friday region;
  - `-u-fw-` (read by the engine only), and `getWeekInfo()` read before `weekInfo`;
  - the `RangeError`;
  - a **parity** case: for every region the runtime names, the regions where the table and the engine disagree must equal exactly the ones a measured ledger (`RELEASE_DELTAS`) records for the runtime's CLDR release, which is none on the table's own release. A rig case and a ledger-honesty case sit beside it;
  - a check that both prototype spellings are restored, because the `unit` project runs `isolate: false`.
- New `packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/CalendarView.weekStartFromLocale-11675.test.tsx` (10 cases):
  - the month grid and its heads under `en-US`, `en-GB`, `zh-CN` and `ar-EG`, and under an authored `locale`;
  - the week view's columns and header range;
  - the wrapped span's title day;
  - the popover under `en-GB` and under `es-MX`, the case where date-fns and CLDR disagree.
- New `packages/plugin-timeline/src/__tests__/ObjectTimeline.weekBucketsFromLocale-11675.test.tsx` (4 cases): the buckets under `en-US`, `en-GB`, `zh-CN` and `ar-EG`.
- Added to the driven zone pin `ObjectTimeline.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`, which `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` already drives: a DST block with a rig case, a fixture-validity case (8 March is 23 hours long there) and the buckets case.
- Re-judged, not weakened: the weekday-head helpers in `CalendarView.gridcellLocale-10144.test.tsx` and `CalendarView.displayLocale-10442.test.tsx` modelled a Sunday-first grid, so they went red under `de` / `de-CH` / `fr-FR`. Their purpose is the heads' language, not their order. They now take the first day as an explicit literal: Monday for `de` / `de-CH` / `fr-FR`, Sunday for `en-US`. Each still asserts the full head row.

## Ablations

Every leg ran through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, from the committed tree. Each leg proved the mutation landed: the anchor count went from 1 to 0 and the blob changed. Each leg proved the restore: the blob matched `HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` was empty. No build was needed: vitest aliases `@object-ui/i18n` to `packages/i18n/src`, and the plugin tests import the components by relative path.

| Leg | Mutation | Predicted | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1a | timeline `daysIntoWeek` hard-coded Monday | `en-US`, `ar-EG` red; `en-GB`, `zh-CN` green | 2 failed / 2 passed, as predicted |
| A1b | `endOfWeek` back to 24-hour steps (zone driver) | the DST case red | the driver's timeline-pin row red; the failing child case is the DST one |
| A1c | `tomorrow` back to `today + 86400000` (zone driver) | the DST case red | same, as predicted |
| A2 | calendar `weekStart` hard-coded 0 | every non-Sunday case red | 11 failed / 8 passed: every non-Sunday case, including the 10144 / 10442 heads; `en-US` and `es-MX` green |
| A2b | popover `weekStartsOn` removed | `es-MX` red | 1 failed: got `lunes`, expected `domingo` |
| A2c | title day back to `getDay() === 0` | the title-day case red | 1 failed, as predicted |
| A3 | CLDR table removed (every region reads Monday) | the table-path cases and parity red | 5 failed / 7 passed |
| A3b | engine path skipped | the `-u-fw-` and `getWeekInfo()` cases red | 2 failed / 10 passed |

## Local verification at `e4f3430`

Every heavy run went through `os-verify-lock.sh`. The exit codes below are the commands' own, captured before any pipe.

- Build: `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-calendar^...' --filter '@object-ui/plugin-timeline^...' build` exited 0. The doc-snippet gate's scoped closure (`turbo run build` over its `--build-filter`) also exited 0: 35 of 35 tasks.
- Tests: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/ packages/plugin-calendar/ packages/plugin-timeline/` exited 0, with 184 files and 2281 tests passed (145 skipped, the driven zone cases among them). `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` exited 0 with 27 passed. That driver counts a skipped child case as a failure, so the new DST cases ran.
- `type-check` for i18n, plugin-calendar and plugin-timeline exited 0. With `--listFiles`, every test file this change touches is in its package's test program.
- `lint` for the same three packages exited 0 (0 errors). The warning counts, by rule, are identical at `daa7caf` and `e4f3430` for `CalendarView.tsx`, `ObjectTimeline.tsx` and the i18n entry files, and every new file has 0 warnings.

  - `check:self-import`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:doc-fences`;
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:shell-escape-residue`;

- NOT MEASURED: `check:node-esm-load`, reason: its provenance leg refused 8 entries that turbo replayed from another worktree's shared cache (auth, core, data-objectstack, mobile, permissions, providers, react-runtime, types). None of them is in this diff, and none of the three touched packages was refused or listed as failing. A clean reading needs `--force-build`, which is CI's whole-tree run.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` belong to CI.

## Patch round 1: CI red on the parity pin at `e4f3430`

**Cause.** CI's `node-version: '22.x'` floats to the newest Node 22, which ships CLDR 48.0. In CLDR 48 Iceland's week starts on Sunday. The table transcribed CLDR 47, where `IS` reads the Monday default, and the pin compared it with whatever CLDR the runtime ships. So the pin was green in a CLDR 47 container and red on CI (`IS: engine 0, table 1`), and updating the table alone would only have moved the red to the CLDR 47 runtime.

**Measured runtimes.** Three official Node builds were run, checksum-verified against nodejs.org's `SHASUMS256.txt`: 22.13.0 (CLDR 46.0, the `engines` floor), 22.22.0 (CLDR 47.0) and 22.23.3 (CLDR 48.0, what CI's `22.x` resolves to). Across the three, `IS` is the only region whose first day differs (Monday, Monday, Sunday).

**Shape chosen: a declared release and an exact-equality ledger.**
- `utils/first-day-of-week.ts` declares the release its table transcribes, `WEEK_DATA_CLDR = '48'`, and the table now carries `IS` on Sunday. All three rows equal the CLDR 48 measurement, region for region.
- The pin reads the runtime's release from the major part of `process.versions.cldr`. The set of regions where the table and the engine disagree must EQUAL `RELEASE_DELTAS[release]`, a ledger in the test whose rows were measured on those runtimes (`46: { IS: Monday }`, `47: { IS: Monday }`). On the table's own release, and on a release the ledger does not list, that set is empty.
- Why equality, not "every disagreement is listed in the delta": a subset check would stay green on a CLDR 46 or 47 runtime if Iceland were reverted in the table, because the disagreement simply disappears there. Equality goes red for that edit on every runtime, and also when a recorded row stops holding.
- Why an empty set for an unlisted release: such a runtime is green when it agrees with the table, and red, naming each region and the remedy, when its CLDR moves a first day. That red is the real drift signal. A new release that moves nothing does not go red.
- Not chosen: skipping the comparison when the release differs. That would turn the pin into a no-op on two of the three supported runtimes.
- What remains: when CI's Node moves to a CLDR release that moves a first day, this pin goes red until the table or the ledger is updated. That is the drift the round asked to keep catching, and the failure message names both remedies.

**Ablations on the new head**, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each with the mutation proven landed and the restore proven (`blob == HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty), and each run on all three runtimes:

| Leg | Mutation | CLDR 46 | CLDR 47 | CLDR 48 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A4 | Iceland removed from the table (back to CLDR 47 content) | red: parity and ledger honesty | red: parity and ledger honesty | red: parity (CI's shape, `{ IS: 0 }` found) and ledger honesty |
| A6 | the ledger's `47` row removed | green | red: `{ IS: 1 }` found, `{}` expected | green |
| A3 | the CLDR table removed | 6 red | 6 red | 6 red |
| A3b | the engine path skipped | 2 red | 2 red | 2 red |

**Re-run at `a393686`** (after merging `main` at `da35453` in `98877dd`, a merge commit; no rebase, no force-push):
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/i18n/ packages/plugin-calendar/ packages/plugin-timeline/` exited 0 on CLDR 47: 184 files, 2283 passed, 145 skipped. The same suites under Node 22.23.3 (CLDR 48, CI's release) exited 0 with the same counts.
- `firstDayOfWeek-11675.test.ts` alone: 14 of 14 passed on CLDR 46, 47 and 48.
- The zone driver `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` exited 0, 27 passed.
- `type-check` and `lint` for the three packages exited 0. The package warning totals are unchanged, and both edited files have 0 warnings.
- `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check:test-path-roots` each exited 0.
- No README, doc or changeset text changed this round, so `check:readme-exports` and `check:doc-snippets` were not re-run.

## Acceptance notes

- **The DST bound correction rides along.** The bucket-bounds block was rewritten as one unit, so `tomorrow` moved from `today + day` to a local-calendar step together with the week bounds. It is pinned by the driven DST case, and ablations A1b and A1c show each half failing alone.
- **The gantt `week` axis is unchanged.** It labels plan weeks (`Week 1`, `Week 2`) counted from the axis's first day, a documented choice, not a hard-coded weekday. Snapping it to a calendar week would change what the axis means. No card.
- **Other date pickers take date-fns's week start.** Pickers outside the calendar, the ones built on the `@object-ui/components` `Calendar` primitive without a `weekStartsOn`, still take date-fns's week start for the tag. For tags date-fns has no locale of its own for (for example `es-MX`), that is not CLDR's start. Ablation A2b measured the mechanism on the primitive, not through a field's public door. Owner: none. Noted, not filed.
- **The table path reads the region only.** A `-u-fw-` or `-u-rg-` keyword on the tag is honoured only where the engine has week info. No producer writes those keywords today.
- **The diff goes beyond the claim's listed file surface in docs only.** The three READMEs, the two `content/docs/plugins` pages and the i18n `index.ts` / `utils/index.ts` exports are required by AGENTS.md #2 or by the helper's own export. They are additive and are named here so the seat can amend the surface.
